description: This topic covers essential keyboard shortcuts used in the Windows Operating System and web browsers. These shortcuts are crucial for increasing efficiency and speed on a computer, making them highly important for competitive exams.

sections.title: Common Windows Shortcuts
sections.description: Crucial daily-use shortcuts for managing documents, files, and system navigation.

key_associations.extra_info: Copies the selected item (text, file, or folder) to the system clipboard.
Removes the selected item from its original location and places it on the clipboard.
Inserts the item from the clipboard to the current active location.
Reverses or undoes your most recent action.
Toggles between currently open applications or active windows.
Closes the active item or exits the active application entirely.

sections.title: Windows Logo Key Shortcuts
sections.description: System-level shortcuts utilized in combination with the Windows logo key (Win).

key_associations.extra_info: Minimizes all open windows immediately to display the computer desktop.
Instantly locks your computer or switches user accounts for security purposes.
Opens the Windows File Explorer to browse and manage files on the system.
Opens the Run command window to execute a program, folder, document, or internet resource.
Opens the Windows Settings app for system configuration and personalization.

sections.title: Web Browser Tabs and Navigation
sections.description: Shortcuts to efficiently manage tabs and navigate within browsers like Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.

key_associations.extra_info: Opens a new blank tab in the current browser window.
Immediately closes the currently active tab you are viewing.
A highly useful shortcut that reopens the last tab that was accidentally closed.
Switches focus to the next open tab on the right side.
Reloads the current webpage to fetch the latest updated data from the server.

sections.title: Web Browser Tools and Page Management
sections.description: Shortcuts for quick access to browser tools like bookmarks, history, and downloads.

key_associations.extra_info: Opens the browsing history tab to view a list of recently visited web pages.
Opens the downloads page to view the list and status of downloaded files.
Saves the URL of the current page as a bookmark for easy access later.
Opens the search bar to find specific text or keywords on the current webpage.
Opens the print dialog box to print the currently displayed webpage.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts and conceptual definitions related to keyboard shortcuts.

key_concepts.explanation: Keys (such as Ctrl, Alt, and Shift) that modify or change the function of another key when pressed together simultaneously.

important_facts.fact: The shortcut 'Win + V' is used to view the Windows Clipboard history, allowing users to see and paste multiple items that were copied previously.
To open an 'Incognito mode' window in Google Chrome for private browsing, the shortcut 'Ctrl + Shift + N' is used.
To open a 'Private window' in Mozilla Firefox or Microsoft Edge, the shortcut 'Ctrl + Shift + P' is utilized.
The shortcut 'Ctrl + Shift + Esc' is the fastest and most direct way to open the Windows Task Manager, which helps in force-closing hung or unresponsive programs.
